label: fixed-tree
rule: payload_pending counts rows the journal holds a signature for but not what happened (logs IS NULL AND payload_state IS NULL)

the default payload-bearing tail HOLDS at that predicate (cursor stays, exit 3, hydrate named) — since v0.7.23 webhook push holds its cursor at it too, hydrate exits 3 while pending_left is non-zero, and the daemon exits 3 at shutdown while the payload hydrate is incomplete
status is the surface a monitoring caller polls; a debt it prints and then calls health is the same lie as a debt it never printed
recorded outcomes (unavailable/invalid) are NOT a debt — hydrate counts them as a completed pass
the opt-in account/owner/account-data queues are not part of the verdict: they drain only behind an opt-in flag and would be a permanent alarm for a default consumer

faces.claim: `status` exits 3 while a row still owes its payload (it prints the count and calls it health)
faces.note: reeflog: 1 row(s) still owe their payload — the journal holds a signature, not what happened; run `reeflog hydrate`

faces.claim: status and the default payload-bearing tail return the SAME exit code for the same journal
faces.note: tail: reeflog: 0 events after cursor 0 → cursor now ? (HELD at seq 1 SIG00000000000000000000000000000000000000001: the payload is still owed — run `hydrate`; nothing at or after this row is consumed)

faces.claim: paying the payload debt flips status back to exit 0 — the verdict tracks the debt
a journal with no debt reports 0 pending and exits 0
faces.note: an exit code that never comes back down is an alarm, not a verdict

faces.claim: rows in a recorded outcome (unavailable/invalid) are NOT a debt: status exits 0
faces.note: the chain forgot these — hydrate counts them as a completed pass, not a pending row

faces.claim: the opt-in queues (accounts/owners/account-data missing) do NOT set the exit code
faces.note: filled only by `hydrate --accounts` and held only behind `tail --with-accounts` — they never drain for a default consumer
